correctness.rationale: Subtracting the centroid gives the stable rate μ=Nκ and a signed linear combination of independent identical harmonic filters. The exact planar single-filter law used is the cited disk law r²/R²∼Beta(1,α). Negating filters 2 through N by isotropy gives positive weights w=( (N−1)/N, 1/N, …, 1/N ). With W=Σw and P=∏w, the radius bound RW is attained as an essential supremum by taking all radii near R and angles near a common direction. The squared triangle deficit is a sum of nonnegative pairwise 1−cos terms; the endpoint event forces every radial deficit to be O(ε) and every principal angular difference from the first to be O(√ε). After removing the common rotation, the weighted-variance angular form has determinant P/W. The scaled event tends to Σx+|z|²/2<1; α>0 makes the bounding density ∏xᵢ^(α−1) integrable on the bounded region. Integrating yields exponent β=Nα+(N−1)/2 and coefficient (2^α Γ(1+α))^N W^(β+1/2)/[(2π)^((N−1)/2) Γ(β+1) P^(α+1/2)], which simplifies to the stated constant. As a separate normalization check, at N=2, α=1 the two-unit-disk overlap area is asymptotic to (4/3)(2−d)^(3/2) at center separation d=2; integrating the radial density 2d times the overlap divided by π from 2(1−ε) to 2 gives 128√2/(15π) times ε^(5/2), in agreement. Source verification notes and code were inspected, not executed; the general Sobol checks at finitely many deficits do not supply a limit proof. The result is fixed finite N, not an assertion of stationary absolute centroid or of a simultaneous large-N edge limit.

evidence: The beta-disk law plus independence gives an exact characteristic-function product. Its existence or abstract radial inversion does not evaluate the near-edge asymptotic.

For comparison, the component projection of the unit beta disk has density proportional to (1−x²)^(α−1/2); positive-deficit convolution gives a projected upper-tail exponent N(α+1/2), not the radial exponent. Obtaining the radial coefficient by this route requires accounting for or inverting the shrinking angular cap.

Random-walk and projection formulations were considered as equivalent derivation routes for the exact problem, not as evidence of a previously established coefficient.

value.rationale: The exact endpoint corrects an unbounded Gaussian outer-tail prediction in a model with bounded active forcing. Beyond the triangle-inequality support bound, the result separates radial persistence cost from the geometric cost of aligning N independent planar vectors and quantifies both in an all-parameter leading coefficient. This gives a finite-population benchmark rather than a statement about crossover or an empirical fit.
